This petition is filed by the petitioner/accused under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., for quashing the FIR in Crime No.28/2024 registered by Magadi Road Police station, Bengaluru for the offences punishable under Sections 181, 419, 420, 465, 466, 468, 471 of IPC.

2. Heard the arguments of learned senior counsel for petitioner and learned HCGP and learned counsel assisting the prosecution.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that one Mohammed Yusuf the District Registrar, Bangalore, filed complaint to the police on 01.02.2024 alleging, that one Sanjeev Mehta said to be furnished documents regarding 15 items of different survey number of lands in respect of GPA dated 27.8.2015, furnished by the petitioner said to be fabricated.

It is further alleged that the GPA has been questioned and as per section 57 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, under Article 41 (e)(b) of Manish Kumar Sethia vs State Of Karnataka on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87288535/

sentences.text: the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, the petitioners deposited Rs.36 lakhs towards the deficit stamp duty and Rs.2 lakhs penalty, totally Rs.38 lakhs under the proceedings were deposited on 26.9.2023 and got released the documents.

The complaint came to be filed by one Sanjeev Mehta, the said documents were forged documents, hence he prayed for taking action against the petitioner as per section 83 of the Registration Act, 1908, if the documents are found to be fake.
After receiving the complaint, the police registered the FIR for the various offences alleged which is under challenge.

4 Learned senior counsel for the petitioner has seriously contended that the FIR registered by the police on the complaint of respondent No.2 is not sustainable since Sanjeev Mehta already filed a complaint before the Doddaballapura Rural Police Station registered in Crime No.6/2024 for the same offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 468, 469, 471 of IPC, based upon the same GPA,
dated 27.8.2015.
Both the FIRs are pertaining to the same transaction, therefore, the present FIR required to be quashed.

5. Learned counsel further contended that as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court Krishna Lal Chawla and Ors Vs State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr., reported in (2021 )5 SCC 435, the second FIR is impermissible.

entities.text: Krishna Lal Chawla and Ors Vs State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr., reported in (2021 )5 SCC 435
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned senior counsel further contended that the petitioner already approached this court for quashing the FIR registered in Doddaballapura Rural Police station which came to be dismissed and permitted to investigate the matter based on the same GPA.
Therefore, once again one more FIR cannot be filed against the petitioner.

Further contended that there is no specific allegation made in the complaint, where the respondent No.2 forwarded the complaint field by the Sanjeev Mehta to the police, which is nothing but a same complaint, which was registered in Doddablalapura police station.
Hence, prayed for quashing the same.
6. Learned senior counsel further contended, the offence punishable under Section 181 of IPC is non cognizable one.
Therefore, there is a bar under Section 195 of Cr.P.C., for filing the FIR, the private complaint required to be filed, therefore, FIR cannot be sustainable.
7. Learned counsel further contended that the offence under Section 181 of IPC required to be filed under the private complaint and the other offences cannot be bifurcated/split up.
Therefore, the FIR is not sustainable.
Hence, prayed for quashing the FIR.
8. Learned Addl. SPP seriously objected the petition contending that the FIR registered in both cases are altogether different.
The petitioner paid the duty and penalty and deficit stamp duty in a proceedings before the Registrar of the Stamps and Registration.
Therefore, the offence committed against proceeding is nothing but a deemed provisions deemed to be judicial proceedings under Section 84 of Registration Act, 1908.
The criminal proceedings can be initiated against the persons for providing false documents.
Hence, prayed for dismissing the petition.

9. Having heard the arguments and perused the records, the case of the prosecution is that, on the complaint of District Registrar Bangalore Rural District, the police registered the FIR for various offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 465, 466, 468, 471 and 181 of IPC.

The main contention of learned senior counsel for the petitioner is that the section 181 of IPC is non cognizable offence and FIR cannot be registered, there is a bar under Section 195 of Cr.P.C. sentences.text: second contention of the learned senior counsel is that there is already one case registered by the Doddaballapura Police Station against the petitioner for the same offences for forging the documents etc., and got registration of the documents before the Sub-Registrar office at Gangenahalli, where FIR has been registered at Doddaballapura Police Station.
Therefore, the second FIR is not sustainable under the law.

10. As regards to the first contention of the learned senior counsel regarding filing of the complaint by the District Registrar, there is a bar for taking cognizance under Section 195 of Cr.P.C. and it is contended that section 181 of IPC cannot be split, with the other IPC cases for registering the FIR or taking the cognizance.

In this regard, learned senior counsel relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bandekar Brothers Pvt., Ltd., Vs Prasad Vassudev Keni and Ors reported in (2020) 20 SCC 1 at paragraph 48 has held as under:

entities.text: Bandekar Brothers Pvt., Ltd., Vs Prasad Vassudev Keni and Ors reported in (2020) 20 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Equally important to remember that if in the course of the same transaction two separate offences are made out, for one of which section 195 of Cr.P.C is not attracted and it is not possible to split them up, the drill of section 195 (1)(b) Cr.P.C must be followed.

Thus in State of Karnataka Vs Hemareddy, this court referred to the judgment of Madras High Court (V.V.L. Narasimhamurthy, In re)"
xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx 8.

We agree with the view expressed by the learned Judge and hold that in cases where in the course of the same transaction an offence for which no complaint by a court is necessary under Section 195(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and an offence for which a complaint of a court is necessary under that sub-section, are committed, it is not possible to split up and hold that the prosecution of the accused for the offences not mentioned in Section 195(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure should be upheld."

11. In view of the said judgment and principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for the offences punishable under Section 181 of IPC, there is a bar under Section 195(1)(b) of Cr.P.C., for filing FIR under Section 154 of Cr.P.C., and the complainant required to file complaint under Section 2(d) read with 200 of Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate.
There is no second opinion in respect of the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

12. On the other hand, the contention of the learned SPP is that the offence punishable under the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 and the Registration Act, 1908, the District Registrar can lodge the complaint, if any offence committed in a proceedings before the Sub-Registrar.

As per the Section 83 of the Registration Act, 1908 which is a s under,
83.
Registering officers may commence prosecutions.-

A prosecution for any offence under this Act coming to the knowledge of a registering officer in his official capacity may be commenced by or with the permission of the Inspector- Manish Kumar Sethia vs State Of Karnataka on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87288535/

(2) Offences punishable under this Act shall be triable by any Court or officer exercising powers not less than those of a Magistrate of the second class.

13. It is relevant to note that the police already registered the FIR against the petitioner at Doddaballapura police station regarding falsifying of the documents and registering the sale deeds in favour of the third parties.
A separate FIR was registered in Doddaballapura Police Station in Crime No.6/2024 on 04.01.2024 which is under investigation.
This court already allowed the police to investigate the matter.

Here in this case, as per section 84 of the Registration Act, 1908, if any proceedings were before the Registering Authority deemed to be public servant and it is judicial proceedings as per section 228 of IPC.

The section 81 of Registration Act, 1908, which is referred as under;
81. Penalty for incorrectly endorsing, copying, translating or registering documents with intent to injure.-Every registering officer appointed under this Act and every person employed in his office for the purposes of this Act,

who, being charged with the endorsing, copying, translating or registering of any document presented or deposited under its provisions, endorses, copies, translates or registers such document in a manner which he knows or believes to be incorrect, intending thereby to cause or knowing it to be likely that he may thereby cause, injury, as defined in the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860), to any person, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

A prosecution for any offence under this Act coming to the knowledge of a registering officer in his official capacity may be commenced by or with a perusal of the section 81 of the Registration Act,
1908, if any document is falsified or produced before the authority and a proceeding took place before the Registrating Authority, which is punishable upto 7 years with fine, which is a cognizable offence is punishable for more than 3 years.

Therefore, under Section 83 of the Registration Act,
1908, the Registrar can launch the prosecution against the person who had produced the false documents.

5 for want of sufficient stamp duty for the purpose of registration.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the registration was made after making deficit stamp duty of Rs.36 lakhs and Rs.2 lakhs penalty total of Rs.38 lakhs were paid by the petitioner in the proceedings held before the District Registrar in impounding the document, the alleged GPA.
Therefore, the proceedings took place before him on fabricated documents.
Therefore, as per section 81 of Registration Act, 1908, petitioner required to be prosecuted by the Registrar which is punishable with 7 years imprisonment.

Therefore, the District Registrar need not file private complaint before the Magistrate for the offences punishable under Section 181 of IPC, but the offence committed was 81 of Registration Act, 1908.
Therefore, merely a wrong provision mentioned by the police in the FIR, that itself is not a ground to quash the FIR.
Therefore, the contention of the learned senior counsel cannot be acceptable, the private complaint shall be filed for the alleged offence.
14. As regards to another contention that Doddabllapur police already registered FIR under Sections 417, 465 and 420 of IPC.
They are doing investigation in Crime No.6/2024
, ofcourse the District Registrar proceedings took place at Rajajinagar Sub- Registrar office, which comes under the Magadi road police station limit.

However, the allegation in respect of the false GPA produced by the accused/petitioner before the Sub-Registrar and got transferred the properties of Sanjeev Mehta and said Mehta also filed complaint to the District Registrar, which is also forwarded to the police.
Therefore, both the investigation required to be done by the same police and FIR cannot be quashed.
On that ground, the contention of the learned senior counsel cannot be acceptable.
The FIR is based upon the same offence cannot be acceptable.
15. The judgment relied by the learned senior counsel is not applicable to the case on hand.
Therefore, the police required to investigate the matter.
However, there will be chances of taking divergent opinion by both the Investigating Officer one at Doddaballapura police station and another at Magadi road police station.

Therefore,
for the purpose of investigation both the FIR shall be investigated by the Doddablallpura police station, where huge property is situated within the limit of Doddaballapura police station.
Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following order; The petition filed by the petitioner is dismissed.

However, the FIR registered by the Magadi road police station in Crime No.24/2024 is ordered to be transferred to Doddaballapura police station to investigate along with Crime No.6/2024 and file the final report in accordance with law.
